name: fastQR
description: Fast QR factorization and updating methods for statistical computations.
methods: QR factorization; updating and downdating; least-squares computations
example: Update a regression fit after adding or removing observations or predictors, and compare the result with a fresh factorization.
scope: Useful when the design changes repeatedly, as in model exploration and sequential analysis.
paper_note: The QR updating paper develops the computational methods underlying this project.

name: fdaSP
description: Functional regression with sparsity-promoting penalties, with examples of estimation, selection and interpretation.
methods: Function-on-scalar and function-on-function regression; sparsity-promoting penalties; MM and ADMM optimization
example: Estimate a functional regression surface and examine where the fitted effect is locally zero, alongside the inflation application in the guide.
scope: Connects sparsity in coefficient functions with interpretable functional regression.
paper_note: The linked papers develop local sparsity for function-on-function and scalar-on-function regression.

name: fastBVS
description: Bayesian variable selection, posterior summaries and model-averaged prediction, supported by fast matrix updates.
methods: Spike-and-slab regression; MCMC; posterior inclusion summaries; model averaging
example: Use the inflation analysis to compare posterior inclusion probabilities, coefficient uncertainty and model-averaged predictions.
scope: Examines uncertainty over competing sparse models rather than reporting a single selected support.
paper_note: The QR updating paper provides related computational background; it is not a separate validation of every fastBVS model.

name: bquantreg
description: Bayesian quantile regression with worked housing-price analyses and comparisons across regression methods.
methods: Gaussian and asymmetric-Laplace quantile models; shrinkage priors; nonlinear, spatial and GMRF effects
example: Follow the independent Munich rental-price and Padova housing-price analyses, progressing from two-regressor models to nonlinear and spatial specifications.
scope: The guide distinguishes conditional means from conditional quantiles and examines posterior uncertainty and computation.

name: SPARES
description: Regularization paths for sparse and adaptive regression, with degrees of freedom and model-selection tools.
methods: Lasso; Group Lasso; overlapping groups; adaptive and sparse-group variants; pathwise complexity and selection tools
example: Compare coefficient paths and local divergence along a regularization grid, then examine how the selection criterion changes with the penalty and adaptive weights.
scope: Combines estimation, prediction and model selection in a common workflow. The public repository hosts the documentation; follow the guide for package installation.
